body: RULE (LOSSES): losses are benign when (1) unit economics are already positive (contribution margin per order/customer/store) and the losses are growth spending or a new segment (Eternal 2022-23; Amazon 1997-2002); (2) the loss is one-time and non-operating (Bharti FY20-21 AGR provision Rs 28,450 cr in one quarter while CFO stayed strong); (3) losses are investee/mark-to-market items around a profitable core (Info Edge). Losses are real when unit economics are negative and worsen with scale, when cash burn needs ever-larger raises, or when the 'path to profit' depends on competitors leaving. RULE (DILUTION): judge by price x purpose x buyer x per-share outcome. Benign: raising at high valuation for high-return growth, ideally small in % terms (Tesla 2020: $12 bn at ~$500 bn, ~1% per raise; Bajaj Finance QIPs at 5-8x book with EPS still up 17x FY15-26; Eternal's Rs 8,500 cr QIP at Rs 252.62 from domestic MFs); rights issues the promoter fully subscribes (Bharti 2019, Reliance 2020). Malignant: equity raised at depressed prices to survive, preferential allotments/warrants to obscure entities, convertible death spirals, heavy SBC (insight:us-redflag-sbc-dilution), or promoter selling into the raise. TEST: per-share metrics net of dilution (EPS, BVPS, FCF/share, 5-year diluted share count CAGR); who bought; use of proceeds vs subsequent capex/ROCE.

data.dilution_benign_if: high price, growth purpose, small %, promoter/strong buyers, per-share metrics rise
data.dilution_malignant_if: low price to survive; obscure preferential; SBC; promoter selling

title: Reading losses and dilution: unit economics, what the money buys, and at what price
